answer: Give every identity weight that grows only with age: a newborn account starts near zero and climbs a slow ridge over many epochs of honest, peer-checked work, so influence is earned in time, not bought in bulk. A gale of fresh fakes arrives weightless — ten thousand new clones together hold less sway than one ivory-tower veteran who has served the network for a year. An attacker can still fake identities, but each must survive months of real contributions before it matters, turning a cheap flood into a long, expensive wait.
